title: Tenant decommission and state cleanup playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the safe, auditable process for decommissioning a tenant (customer/namespace) from a Redwood Private deployment. It covers the operator steps to: quiesce traffic, snapshot and export required state, scrub or purge customer data, revoke secrets, reconcile billing records, and verify rollout safety. The goal is to avoid data loss for active customers, preserve evidence for compliance requests, and ensure capacity and licensing are reclaimed cleanly.

Scope
-----
- Applies to private/VPC and on-prem tenant deployments (single-tenant and multi-tenant partitions).
- Covers tenants that are being: fully deprovisioned (end of contract), moved to another region/operator, or merged.
- Does NOT cover ephemeral test tenants that follow a shorter teardown flow.

Stakeholders and ownership
-------------------------
- Requestor: Customer Success (initiates decommission request and holds signed AOR).
- Primary operator: Tenant Ops (oncall team).
- Secondary: Security & Compliance (evidence retention), Billing (final invoice), Platform SRE (capacity reclamation), Field Eng (if model license entanglement exists).

Key SLOs and constraints
-------------------------
- Customer-visible downtime: Target 2h for planned decommissions, can be extended with agreement.
- Evidence retention window: As per contract (typical minimum 90 days); see customer contract for exact retention.
- Secure purge verification: Cryptographic checksums for exported snapshots must be recorded and stored in evidence bundle.

Preflight checklist (operator must verify before starting)
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Signed decommission authorization received and attached to ticket (CS ticket ID).
2. Contract retention and deletion policy confirmed with Compliance.
3. Backup snapshot policy — target retention and export destinations verified.
4. Active sessions and in-flight requests drained or scheduled for customer notification window.
5. Escrowed model licensing or vendor entitlements identified.
6. Billing reconciliation tasks created and assigned.

Runbook: step-by-step procedure
-------------------------------
1) Prepare the environment
   - Assign a single operator owner and a verifier. Record names in ticket.
   - Set maintenance window in status page and notify CS to notify customer.
   - Create an evidence bundle: ticket export, contract excerpt, operator checklist (use template).

2) Quiesce traffic and freeze writes
   - Put tenant routes into read-only or maintenance mode via operator API:

     $ redwood-admin tenant set-mode --tenant <TENANT_ID> --mode maintenance

   - Verify no new writes for 15 minutes and monitor request rate.

3) Consistent snapshot and export
   - Trigger state snapshot for the following components: model KV cache, tenant metadata, embeddings index, upload storage (S3/GCS), and config store.
   - Snapshot-specific example (CLI):

     $ redwood-admin snapshot create --tenant <TENANT_ID> --components kv,embeddings,uploads,config --region us-west-2

   - Copy snapshots to the approved export bucket with server-side encryption and immutable retention (if contract requires). Record object names and checksums.

4) Validate exported data (evidence step)
   - Compute and record SHA256 checksums for each exported artifact and store in evidence bundle.
   - Run quick integrity verification: restore snapshot into a temporary verification namespace (read-only) and run smoke prompts against a fixed eval set to validate model-state bindings.

5) Secrets and key management
   - Revoke tenant-scoped API keys and rotate any shared keys used by the tenant.
   - If customer provided KMS keys, coordinate HSM/KMS rotation or destruction per contract. Record KMS transaction IDs.

6) Data purge or archive
   - If contract states purge: perform secure delete on object stores and database rows using provider best-practices (e.g., S3 object deletion + overwrite if required for air-gapped environment).
   - If contract states archive: move data to contract archive bucket and apply access controls.

7) License and model entitlement cleanup
   - Remove tenant binding from any licensed model entitlements. Notify Model Ops that capacity has been reclaimed.

8) Reclaim compute and network resources
   - Drain and deallocate tenant-specific GPU pools and ephemeral volumes. Verify volumes are detached.

9) Billing and ticket closure
   - Create final invoice entry and confirm with Billing. Attach evidence bundle and signed confirmation.
   - Mark ticket as ready for closure and route to CS for final customer signoff.

10) Post-decommission verification (7 and 30 days)
   - 7-day check: Ensure no reappearance of tenant routes/keys and no access events in audit log.
   - 30-day audit: Compliance to review evidence bundle and confirm retention timeline or final purge.

Operator checklist (copy into ticket)
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Maintenance window announced and recorded
- [ ] Evidence bundle created (ticket snapshot + contract)
- [ ] Mode set to maintenance and writes frozen
- [ ] Snapshots exported and checksums recorded
- [ ] Temporary verification namespace validated
- [ ] Tenant API keys revoked and KMS ops recorded
- [ ] Data purge/archive completed and access controls applied
- [ ] Licenses & entitlements released
- [ ] Compute & storage deallocated
- [ ] Billing reconciliation completed
- [ ] CS signoff recorded

Automation snippets and examples
-------------------------------
- Example JSON payload to request a snapshot via internal API:

  {
    "tenant_id": "<TENANT_ID>",
    "components": ["kv","embeddings","uploads","config"],
    "export_bucket": "s3://redwood-exports/private-tenant-archive",
    "encryption": "aws:kms",
    "immutable_retention_days": 90
  }

- Example playbook job (Kubernetes Job spec) to run export in-cluster: use job name prefix tenant-decomm-<TENANT_ID>. The operator must set node selector for non-preemptible nodes.

Safety and rollback procedures
------------------------------
- If a destructive step (purge) was run prematurely, follow emergency rollback:
  1. Immediately stop further deletions and escalate to Security.
  2. Restore from last verified snapshot to temporary namespace for forensic inspection.
  3. Notify Billing and CS of possible data loss and freeze closure.
  4. If customer is in-contract with recovery SLA, execute recovery workflow and update ticket timeline.

- Non-destructive recoveries (re-enable tenant):
  - Rebind route, re-issue API keys, and re-provision resources from preserved snapshots. Document all changes and require dual-operator signoff.

Verification and audit artifacts (what to store in evidence bundle)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Decommission authorization (signed PDF), ticket ID, operator names and timestamps.
- Snapshot manifests and checksums (SHA256).
- KMS transaction IDs and revoked key lists.
- Billing reconciliation export and final invoice ID.
- Audit log extracts (start/end) covering maintenance window.
- Smoke test results from verification namespace.

Table: required export components and retention guidance
--------------------------------------------------------
| Component         | Minimum export items                        | Suggested retention |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Uploads (S3/GCS)  | Object listing, object tar/manifest, checksums | 90 days / contract |
| KV cache state    | Serialized snapshot, TTL map, metadata      | 30 days            |
| Embeddings index  | Vector payload, index schema, metadata      | 90 days / archive  |
| Config store      | Full config dump (YAML/JSON), ACLs          | 365 days (config)  |
| Audit logs        | Event window covering 7 days prior to decomm | 365 days           |

Postmortem triggers (automated)
--------------------------------
- Unexpected 5xx spike during maintenance window > 1 minute.
- Any failed verification smoke test.
- Missing or mismatched checksum on exported artifact.

Common failure modes and mitigations
------------------------------------
- Large export timeouts: use multipart exports and parallelize by prefix; extend maintenance window.
- KMS key rotation collisions: always coordinate with Compliance and vendor before rotate.
- Billing mismatch: hold final invoice until evidence bundle validated.

Appendix A: Templates and CLI references
---------------------------------------
- Evidence bundle template: /templates/decomm-evidence-bundle.md
- Snapshot CLI: redwood-admin snapshot create --help
- Verification playbook: /playbooks/tenant-snapshot-verify.yaml

Appendix B: Operator escalation matrix
-------------------------------------
- Tier 1 (Tenant Ops): Oncall owner (30m response)
- Tier 2 (Platform SRE): Pager duty (1h response)
- Tier 3 (Security/Compliance): Email + pager (2h response)
